name: azure_node_pool
description:
Manages a node pool (AKS agent pool) on an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster, provisioned within an environment and resource group.

The pool is created on the AKS cluster linked to the resource group, so that resource group must already have a cluster attached and the cluster must have finished provisioning — the API rejects the create otherwise. Every pool is created as a `User` pool backed by a virtual machine scale set; the cluster's own system pool is not managed here.

The platform stores the pool's configuration and sends the whole of it to Azure on every change, so Terraform sends every field back on update, not just the ones that changed. Nothing in this resource surfaces live Azure state such as the current node count or Kubernetes version: the API deliberately withholds the raw cloud snapshot from its responses, so only `arm_resource_id` and the platform's own status are available. The record's version counter and last-updated timestamp are not exposed either — the API refreshes its cloud snapshot on every read and saves the record as it does, so both change on every GET and would report drift on every plan while meaning nothing.

invalidWhen.message: min_count must be at least 1 when enable_auto_scaling is true — the AKS autoscaler cannot scale a pool to zero nodes.
max_count must be greater than or equal to min_count when enable_auto_scaling is true. Note both default to 1, so setting only min_count leaves max_count below it.
upgrade_settings cannot have both surge and unavailable active: Azure accepts only one. Leave one type as Default, or set its value to 0.

attributes.name: workspace_id
attributes.description: ID of the workspace that owns this node pool.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Node pool name. 1-12 characters, lowercase letters and digits only — no hyphens, underscores or capitals. A Windows pool is limited to 6 characters, which Azure enforces. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: environment_id
attributes.description: ID of the environment in which the node pool is provisioned.

attributes.name: resource_group_id
attributes.description: ID of the resource group in which the node pool is provisioned. The AKS cluster the pool joins is the one linked to this resource group.

attributes.name: scope_ids
attributes.description: Scope IDs linking this node pool to a cloud provider account, inherited from the resource group.

attributes.name: vm_size
attributes.description: Azure VM size for the pool's nodes, e.g. `Standard_DS2_v2`. Immutable after creation — Azure has no way to resize an existing pool, so changing this replaces it. Which sizes are available depends on the subscription and region.

attributes.name: os_type
attributes.description: Operating system for the pool's nodes. Immutable after creation. A `Windows` pool additionally caps `name` at 6 characters.

attributes.name: os_sku
attributes.description: Specific OS image for the pool's nodes. Left unset, Azure picks the default for `os_type` — currently Ubuntu for Linux and Windows2022 for Windows. Must match `os_type`: the Windows SKUs are only valid on a Windows pool, `Ubuntu` and `AzureLinux` only on a Linux one. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: availability_zones
attributes.description: Availability zones the pool spreads its nodes across, e.g. `["1", "2", "3"]`. Left unset, the pool is not zone-spanning. Only zones the region actually offers are accepted. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: scale_set_priority
attributes.description: Pricing tier for the pool's scale set. `Spot` nodes cost less but Azure can evict them at any time, so keep interruption-tolerant workloads on them only. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: max_pods_per_node
attributes.description: Maximum pods that may be scheduled on each node. Immutable after creation, and bounded by the cluster's network plugin — the practical ceiling is 250, and Azure CNI reserves an IP address per pod, so a high value needs a subnet large enough to cover `max_pods_per_node` × nodes.

attributes.name: node_count
attributes.description:
Number of nodes in the pool. Ignored while `enable_auto_scaling` is true — Azure then drives the count itself between `min_count` and `max_count`, and a value set here is not applied.

Named `node_count` rather than `count` because `count` is a reserved Terraform meta-argument.

attributes.name: min_count
attributes.description: Lower bound for the autoscaler. Only meaningful when `enable_auto_scaling` is true, and must then be at least 1.

attributes.name: max_count
attributes.description: Upper bound for the autoscaler. Only meaningful when `enable_auto_scaling` is true, and must then be greater than or equal to `min_count`.

attributes.name: enable_auto_scaling
attributes.description: Let the AKS cluster autoscaler size the pool between `min_count` and `max_count`. While enabled, `node_count` has no effect.

attributes.name: allocation_tag
attributes.description: Workload allocation tag for the pool. The platform turns it into an `allocationtags` node label, which is how a service is pinned to these nodes. Must be a valid Kubernetes label value: at most 63 characters of letters, digits, dashes, underscores and dots, starting and ending alphanumeric. Clearing it removes the label.

attributes.name: node_labels
attributes.description: Kubernetes labels applied to every node in the pool. The platform adds its own `resourcegroup`, `environment`, `workspace` and `allocationtags` labels so that pods can target these nodes; those are filtered out of state and always win over a value set here, so use `allocation_tag` rather than writing the `allocationtags` label directly.

attributes.name: node_taints
attributes.description: Kubernetes taints applied to every node in the pool, so only pods with a matching toleration are scheduled there.

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: Taint key.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Taint value.

attributes.name: effect
attributes.description: What the taint does to pods that do not tolerate it. `NoSchedule` keeps new pods off the node, `PreferNoSchedule` avoids it when possible, and `NoExecute` also evicts pods already running there.

attributes.name: upgrade_settings
attributes.description: How aggressively Azure rolls nodes during an upgrade. At most one of surge or unavailable may be active: the API rejects a setting where both are greater than zero.

attributes.name: max_surge_type
attributes.description: How `max_surge_value` is read. `Default` leaves surge to Azure and ignores the value.

attributes.name: max_surge_value
attributes.description: Extra nodes Azure may add during an upgrade — a node count, or a percentage of the pool between 0 and 100. Required when `max_surge_type` is not `Default`.

attributes.name: max_unavailable_type
attributes.description: How `max_unavailable_value` is read. `Default` leaves it to Azure and ignores the value.

attributes.name: max_unavailable_value
attributes.description: Nodes Azure may take out of service at once during an upgrade — a node count, or a percentage of the pool between 0 and 100. Required when `max_unavailable_type` is not `Default`.

attributes.name: provisioner_type
attributes.description: Provisioner type. Assigned by the platform when unset.

attributes.name: provisioner_version
attributes.description: Optional provisioner version. Left unset the API omits it, so this reads back empty rather than as an empty string.

attributes.name: cluster_id
attributes.description: ID of the cluster this pool belongs to, taken from the resource group's linked cluster when the pool is created.

attributes.name: azure_cluster_name
attributes.description: Name of the AKS managed cluster in Azure that hosts this pool.

attributes.name: azure_cluster_resource_group_name
attributes.description: Azure resource group that owns the AKS managed cluster. Note this is the cluster's resource group, which is not necessarily the one named by `resource_group_id`.

attributes.name: unique_cloud_resource_id
attributes.description: Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the node pool, as the platform records it on the resource itself. It is what the delete and refresh operations use to reach the pool. `arm_resource_id` exposes the same ID as reported after creation.

attributes.name: node_pool_id
attributes.description: ID of this node pool, for reference by dependent resources.

attributes.name: arm_resource_id
attributes.description: Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the node pool, as reported after creation.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current provisioning status of the node pool.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when the node pool was created (RFC 3339).
